raw_response:
I'm 38 years old, farming these 20 mu in Quzhou County for 10 years now. I finished middle school, so I can read the instructions on fertilizer bags and understand most of what the extension technician says, but honestly I trust what I see in my own fields more than what I read in a book. My household has six people—my parents, my wife, our two school-age children, and me. My younger brother works construction in the county town and sends money home when he can, which helps with cash, but I still have to be careful. We live on this land.

I just finished getting the summer maize out a few days ago—about 480 kg per mu, which was acceptable though not great. The weather was a bit dry in August. Now the clock is ticking: I need to plant winter wheat by mid-October at the latest, or the seedlings won't survive the winter well.

**Winter wheat (20 mu):** I'm planting around October 10th. I'm buying improved seed from the supply store—probably Jimai 22 or something similar, about 40 yuan per mu. I don't save my own seed anymore; two years ago the germination was poor and I learned my lesson. For fertilizer, the extension technician keeps saying 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is the scientific rate, but I've always used a bit more to be safe. Last year I cut back to try to save money and the wheat looked yellow at jointing. Never again. I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as a base before planting, then topdress with 20 kg of urea at jointing in March. That's about 16 kg of nitrogen total per mu. The compound gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, about 6 kg each. I thought about soil testing, but the test costs money and I know my land by now.

For water, I'll irrigate three times: once before winter if the rain doesn't come, once at jointing in late March, and once at flowering in late April. Each time costs about 15–20 yuan per mu in electricity for the pump. Three times is enough—more than that and I'm just throwing money into the well. I'll spray herbicide in early spring for the wild oats; the chemical costs about 12 yuan per mu.

I hire Old Zhang from the east end of the village for rotary tillage and planting. I don't own a tractor—20 mu isn't quite enough to justify one. Tillage and planting together cost about 55 yuan per mu. Harvesting in June I'll hire a combine.

**Summer maize (20 mu):** The wheat comes off around June 8th–12th, and I need to get the maize in the ground within a week or the yield drops. I'll plant around June 12th using hybrid seed—Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958, whatever the store has in stock. Costs about 50 yuan per mu. The window is tight, so I keep tillage simple: light rotary tillage into the wheat stubble, then straight in with the planter.

For maize fertilizer, I'll spread 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and if I have time during the summer rush I'll topdress 20 kg of urea at the big trumpet stage. If my brother isn't back from town to help, I might skip the topdressing and just accept slightly lower yield. That's roughly 14–15 kg of nitrogen per mu. Water for maize: I'll plan on two irrigations, at tasseling and grain filling, but if July brings good rain I might get away with one. Electricity is expensive.

For chemicals, maize needs herbicide at seedling stage for sure, and I usually keep one insecticide spray ready for armyworms in July—if I see them, I spray immediately.

**Labor and cash:** Most work is me, my wife, and my father. My mother watches the children and cooks. During harvest and planting rush, I'll hire two or three laborers for a couple of days each time. I budget about 16,000 yuan total for inputs this year—seed, fertilizer, chemicals, water, machine hire, and hired labor. That's almost all my liquid cash. My wife worries, but what else can we do? You have to spend money to make money, though I'd rather be a little safe than sorry. If I get 420 kg per mu of wheat and 480 kg per mu of maize, we'll break even and have some left for the kids' school fees. That's all I ask.
